card.description: A planar CSS stabilizer code obtained by putting qubits on the edges of a cellulated surface, X checks at vertices, and Z checks around faces. Rough and smooth boundaries absorb the two kinds of error string; a string that joins the complementary boundaries is logical. This unrotated family is constructed exactly as HGP(rep_L, rep_L).

views.description: Expanding the two repetition-factor boundary maps gives sparse binary X and Z check matrices. Their stacked symplectic rows are the universal executable baseline used for commutation, rank, logical, and distance calculations.

Two open length-L repetition chains form the two axes. The two HGP qubit blocks are bit×bit and check×check, while X and Z checks let one parity map act at a time; open-chain corank is exactly what leaves one logical qubit rather than the toric code's two.

The checks are the boundary and coboundary maps of a relative chain complex. Logical strings are relative cycles modulo boundaries, and distance is the shortest nontrivial primal or dual relative cycle.

Error chains with a fixed syndrome become disorder sectors of a random-bond Ising model. Maximum-likelihood decoding compares their free energies; minimum-weight matching is the zero-temperature approximation that keeps energy but discards path entropy.

A phase-free ZX diagram and a CSS code encode the same binary linear subspace. In this language rough/smooth merge and split operations become spider maps, so lattice surgery is diagram rewriting rather than an opaque stabilizer schedule.

The toric bulk underlying the planar patch becomes a quantized graph: star and plaquette checks are unified as cycle operators, e/m duality is graph self-duality, and charged string diagrams expose the fermionic composite and twist-defect bookkeeping.

The ground space is a PEPS whose virtual Z2 symmetry generates topological degeneracy, local indistinguishability, and anyonic excitations. The code's topological order is therefore a constraint on the local tensor, not merely a property asserted from its Hamiltonian.

decoders.noise: independent X/Z noise with perfect syndrome (code capacity)
decoders.notes: Matching reaches about 10.3%, while maximum-likelihood decoding reaches about 10.9% under the corresponding independent-noise convention. The gap is path entropy: matching minimizes chain energy rather than class free energy.

decoders.noise: phenomenological data and syndrome noise over repeated rounds
decoders.notes: The spacetime matching transition is about 2.9% for the symmetric phenomenological model studied by Wang, Harrington, and Preskill. This number is not a circuit-level gate threshold.

Fowler's scheduled eight-step syndrome circuit has a threshold near 0.57% per circuit step, or roughly 4% per full cycle in that paper's stochastic model. The value is schedule-, gate-set-, and decoder-dependent, so it must not be compared directly with the code-capacity figures above.

decoders.noise: perfect syndrome and faulty repeated syndrome benchmarks
decoders.notes: The toric-bulk benchmarks give about 9.9% with perfect syndrome and 2.6% with faulty syndrome measurements. Union-find trades a small threshold loss relative to matching for almost-linear worst-case processing.

decoders.noise: code-capacity Pauli noise on surface/toric-code lattices
decoders.notes: Hierarchical coarse-graining estimates the probability of logical classes rather than committing immediately to one globally lightest chain. It exposes a distinct speed/accuracy tradeoff and generalizes naturally to other topological-code lattices.

decoders.noise: independent X/Z noise exactly; general Pauli noise approximately
decoders.notes: Exact free-fermion contraction is available for the restricted independent channel, while matrix-product-state contraction approximates maximum likelihood for more general noise. The bond dimension controls the accuracy/runtime tradeoff.

decoders.noise: CSS parity-check decoding with calibrated soft information
decoders.notes: Belief propagation supplies qubit reliabilities and ordered-statistics post-processing repairs non-convergence on the lattice's short cycles. It is a portable qLDPC baseline rather than a geometry-specialized decoder.

Belief propagation first assigns correlated fault mechanisms to detector events, then reweights a matching graph. This retains the mature matching backend while correcting the independent-edge approximation.

realizations.description: Scaling from distance 3 to distance 5 reduced logical error per cycle from the distance-3 ensemble average 3.028% ± 0.023% to 2.914% ± 0.016%. This is the 2023 distance-scaling result; it did not report the later Willow suppression factor.
A distance-7 patch reached 0.143% ± 0.003% logical error per cycle and each distance increase of two suppressed error by Λ = 2.14 ± 0.02, with logical lifetime beyond the best physical qubit.

Hexagonal-connectivity, walking data/measure-role, and iSWAP-based surface-code schedules all showed distance-dependent error suppression, demonstrating that the code can be adapted to connectivity, leakage, and native-gate constraints.
A 17-qubit distance-3 Surface-17 patch executed repeated correction cycles, providing an independent superconducting realization of a planar surface-code memory.

Movable atoms realized surface-code patches inside a multi-code logical processor and enabled transversal inter-patch entangling gates by aligning corresponding data qubits. This is a logical-operations demonstration, not a below-threshold surface-memory claim; for the distance-five and distance-seven surface blocks, logical input-state preparation was not itself fault-tolerant.

relations.how: HGP(rep_L, rep_L) — the planar surface code is the hypergraph product of two repetition codes
The same square-lattice star/plaquette bulk is obtained from HGP(rep_L, rep_L); open repetition factors give the planar Surface patch, while periodic factors close it into the toric code.

operations.cost: O(d) rounds per merge/split plus an ancilla routing patch
constant-depth physical CNOT layer; transport and correlated-decoding costs remain
O(d) or more rounds and a distance-sized reserved hole trajectory
twist/corner code deformation over distance-preserving paths
constant-depth gates plus a fold or equivalent qubit permutation
prepare a physical product state, measure the complementary stabilizers for d rounds, and decode the spacetime record
destructively measure all data qubits in the selected basis and decode the final data/syndrome history
a classical frame update after decoded logical measurements; no immediate physical Pauli layer is required
inject and distill a magic state, then consume it by gate teleportation; factory spacetime dominates

# Surface code (planar, unrotated)

## Essence

**The object.** Put data qubits on the even-even and odd-odd sites of a
`(2L−1) × (2L−1)` checkerboard. The two blocks contain `L²` and `(L−1)²`
qubits. Put X-checks on the even-odd sites and Z-checks on the odd-even
sites; a check acts on the data qubits one lattice step away. Interior checks
have weight four and boundary checks have weight three. The resulting family
has

`[[2L²−2L+1, 1, L]]`.

The shipped instances are `[[13,1,3]]`, `[[25,1,4]]`, and `[[41,1,5]]`.
The verifier recomputes `n` and `k` for all three, enumerates `d=3,4`
exactly, and reruns a seeded weight-five upper-bound witness for `L=5`; the
matching lower bound is literature-backed. The complete calculation is in
[the HGP construction transcript](pedagogy/hgp-construction.md) and
[the distance proof](pedagogy/distance-proof.md).

**The idea.** A repetition code stores one observable nonlocally and leaves
its conjugate local: with checks `Z_i Z_{i+1}`, one can choose
`X_L=X⊗...⊗X` but `Z_L=Z_1`. In the Ising picture, a one-site order
parameter distinguishes the two ground states. That is fatal for a quantum
memory: the [Knill–Laflamme condition](../../foundations/knill-laflamme/)
requires every operator supported in a correctable region to act as a scalar
inside the code space.

Gauging the Ising `Z₂` symmetry replaces the local order parameter by a local
constraint. Qubits live on square-lattice edges; a star
`A_v=∏_{e∋v}X_e` imposes the Gauss law and a plaquette
`B_p=∏_{e∈∂p}Z_e` imposes zero flux. At this commuting-projector fixed
point, every sufficiently local operator has only scalar matrix elements
within the ground space, while nontrivial encoded action requires a
noncontractible string. On a torus there are two independent string qubits.
Cutting to a disk with two rough and two smooth boundary segments leaves one.
This is the planar surface code introduced through lattice boundaries by
[Bravyi and Kitaev](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9811052), built from
Kitaev's [`Z₂` topological code](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9707021).

**One sentence.** The surface code is the repetition code with its local
order parameter gauged away, then cut so that one conjugate pair of
boundary-to-boundary strings survives.

## Design problem

A distance-`d` quantum code detects every Pauli error of weight below `d` and
corrects arbitrary errors on at most `⌊(d−1)/2⌋` unknown qubits. It must
therefore protect both X-like and Z-like directions. Concatenated codes do
this recursively, and the threshold theorem proves that sufficiently weak
local noise can be suppressed to arbitrary accuracy
([Aharonov–Ben-Or](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9906129)).

The engineering problem is not whether concatenation works, but what
interaction contract its recursive gadgets impose. Higher levels require
protected inner gadgets, verified ancillas, and either long-range
connectivity or routing. The surface-code alternative is to hold the
microscopic contract fixed:

- check weight stays at most four;
- interactions stay nearest-neighbor in two dimensions;
- one syndrome round has constant circuit depth;
- protection grows only by enlarging the patch.

This locality makes repeated measurement natural and turns decoding into a
bulk phase-transition problem. It also imposes two unavoidable prices.
First, two-dimensional commuting local checks obey the
[Bravyi–Poulin–Terhal tradeoff](../../foundations/bounds/bravyi-poulin-terhal.md),
`k d² = O(n)`. Second, bounded-spread local logical gates in two dimensions
are Clifford by the
[Bravyi–König theorem](../../foundations/bounds/bravyi-koenig.md), so a
native logical T gate is unavailable. The surface code is the answer to a
specific design choice: pay geometric area and magic-state overhead in
exchange for a local syndrome circuit with a reachable threshold.

## Derivation chain

**Physical route: gauge, close, then cut.**

1. The repetition/Ising code has a weight-one order parameter. Gauging its
   global `Z₂` symmetry gives edge qubits with star and plaquette constraints.
2. On an `L × L` torus there are `2L²` edge qubits. The `L²` stars have one
   product relation and so do the `L²` plaquettes, giving
   `k=2L²−(2L²−2)=2`. The logicals are the two homologically nontrivial loop
   classes and their duals.
3. A rough boundary condenses the electric endpoint of a Z string; a smooth
   boundary condenses the magnetic endpoint of an X string. A disk with only
   one boundary type has no protected string qubit. Alternating two rough and
   two smooth segments leaves a vertical Z class and a horizontal X class,
   which cross once and anticommute.
4. In the shipped geometry, top and bottom are rough and left and right are
   smooth. The [computed syndrome walk](pedagogy/syndrome-decoding.md) shows
   a bulk error producing two defects, a boundary absorbing one endpoint,
   and a completed crossing string producing no syndrome.

**Algebraic route: hypergraph product of two open chains.**

Let `H` be the `(L−1) × L` repetition parity matrix with adjacent `11`
rows. For two copies, the constructor forms

`H_X = [H ⊗ I_L | I_(L−1) ⊗ Hᵀ]`,

`H_Z = [I_L ⊗ H | Hᵀ ⊗ I_(L−1)]`.

The two qubit blocks contain `L²` bit×bit coordinates and `(L−1)²`
check×check coordinates. Commutation is designed in:

`H_X H_Zᵀ = H ⊗ Hᵀ + H ⊗ Hᵀ = 0` over `F₂`.

The open-chain matrix has rank `L−1`, hence classical dimensions
`k=1` and `kᵀ=0`. The HGP dimension formula
`k_Q=k₁k₂+k₁ᵀk₂ᵀ` therefore gives one logical qubit. Closing each chain
adds a dependent parity row: `kᵀ` becomes one and the same product gives the
toric code's two logical qubits. Thus “boundary versus handle” is the
corank of the classical factor matrix, not a metaphor.

The geometric checkerboard is exactly these Kronecker blocks laid out in the
plane. The [worked HGP page](pedagogy/hgp-construction.md) prints the matrices,
coordinate dictionary, locality checks, ranks, and commutation cancellation
from the shipped constructor.

## Multiple pictures

- **Homology.** `H_Zᵀ` and `H_X` are consecutive boundary maps. Z-logicals
  are relative cycles modulo face boundaries; X-logicals are the dual
  relative cycles. Multiplying by a stabilizer deforms a string within its
  relative homology class. Distance is the shortest nontrivial primal or dual
  relative cycle. See the
  [CSS chain-complex dictionary](../../foundations/css-chain-complexes/).

- **Anyons and decoding.** An error chain's syndrome is its boundary.
  Decoding chooses another chain with the same boundary; error plus
  correction is harmless exactly when the resulting cycle is homologically
  trivial. Maximum-likelihood decoding compares the total probability of
  homology classes, whereas minimum-weight matching keeps the lightest chain.
  The [syndrome page](pedagogy/syndrome-decoding.md) derives this statement,
  and the [threshold ledger](pedagogy/threshold-ledger.md) keeps the
  code-capacity, phenomenological, and circuit-level numbers separate.

- **Circuits and detectors.** A standard check measurement prepares one
  ancilla, entangles it with neighboring data qubits, and measures it. A
  detector is usually the parity of consecutive outcomes of the same check.
  Relevant single faults produce small detector patterns; some circuit faults
  are benign or observationally equivalent, so “every fault lights a
  detector” would be too strong. CNOT order matters because an ancilla fault
  can propagate to a two-data-qubit hook; the schedule must orient hooks away
  from the shortest logical direction.

- **Rotated cut.** The unrotated patch uses
  `2d²−2d+1` data qubits. Recutting the same bulk by 45 degrees puts the data
  on a `d × d` array while keeping both crossing lengths equal to `d`, giving
  `[[d²,1,d]]`. With one dedicated check ancilla per independent stabilizer,
  the totals are respectively `4d²−4d+1` and `2d²−1`. The saving is boundary
  geometry, not a new phase; the rotated construction is described explicitly
  in [Horsman et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.4022).

- **XZZX under biased noise.** A Hadamard on alternating data qubits maps the
  CSS presentation to XZZX checks. Under pure Z noise, XZZX defects obey
  separate parity constraints along diagonals, reducing decoding to
  independent repetition-code problems and giving a 50% code-capacity
  threshold. In the ordinary CSS presentation, pure Z errors trigger only
  X-checks—one syndrome graph—but that graph remains two-dimensional. The
  advantage is the XZZX diagonal conservation law, not a reduction from two
  CSS graphs to one. This mechanism and its finite-bias limits are derived in
  [Bonilla Ataides et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.07851).

- **Fermions and twists.** Star and plaquette defects are the `e` and `m`
  anyons. Moving one around the other produces a minus sign, so their
  composite has fermionic self-statistics. An `e↔m` duality wall can end at a
  twist defect; the patch corners are boundary-changing versions of the same
  object. This is why twist encodings inherit Majorana-like fusion
  bookkeeping without containing microscopic Majorana particles.

- **Laboratory memory.** Google's distance-five memory slightly outperformed
  distance three in the
  [2023 experiment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.06431). The later
  [distance-seven experiment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.13687) measured
  `0.143% ± 0.003%` logical error per cycle and an empirical suppression
  factor `Λ=2.14 ± 0.02` for a distance increase of two. `Λ` is a
  device-and-decoder fit, not a direct measurement of `p_th/p`.

## Why these parameters

**Length.** The HGP has one `L²` qubit block and one `(L−1)²` block, so
`n=2L²−2L+1`. The constructor and verifier recompute this for every shipped
instance.

**Dimension.** Each open repetition matrix has `k=1` and transpose dimension
zero. Künneth bookkeeping gives `1·1+0·0=1`. Direct rank computation agrees:
both quantum check matrices have rank `L(L−1)`, hence
`k=n−2L(L−1)=1`.

**Distance.** A row of the `L × L` block is an X-logical and a column is a
Z-logical, so `d≤L`. For the reverse inequality, the Z-logical class has `L`
pairwise-disjoint column representatives, all equivalent modulo
Z-stabilizers. Any logical anticommuting with that class must touch every one
of those disjoint supports and therefore has weight at least `L`; the same
argument with the X rows handles the conjugate class. Thus `d=L`. The
[distance page](pedagogy/distance-proof.md) proves the general statement and
then checks the representatives computationally.

**Verification status.** `L=3,4` use exhaustive CSS logical enumeration.
For `L=5`, the lower bound `d≥5` is carried by the family theorem and its
literature provenance, while the verifier reruns a seeded low-weight search
that finds a weight-five logical. The instance is therefore marked
`bounded`, not `verified`.

**Rate and locality.** `k/n→0` while `d=Θ(√n)`. This saturates the
two-dimensional `k d²=O(n)` tradeoff up to a constant. The complete argument,
including exactly where Euclidean bounded range enters, lives on the
[BPT derivation page](../../foundations/bounds/bravyi-poulin-terhal.md).
Likewise, the absence of a constant-depth local T gate follows from the
[full Bravyi–König derivation](../../foundations/bounds/bravyi-koenig.md),
not from a slogan about transversality.

## Failure modes

- **Area overhead.** For this unrotated family, one check ancilla per
  independent stabilizer gives `4d²−4d+1` physical qubits per logical
  memory. The rotated patch reduces this to `2d²−1`. These totals exclude
  routing lanes, spare qubits, and factory space, which must be stated
  separately rather than hidden in “physical qubits.”

- **No passive thermal memory.** A logical string can grow while paying only
  for its pointlike endpoints, so the commuting Hamiltonian has an
  order-one energy barrier. Two-dimensional local stabilizer Hamiltonians
  cannot be self-correcting
  ([Bravyi–Terhal](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.1983)); continuous active
  measurement is part of the memory, not an optional implementation detail.

- **Decoder/model dependence.** Minimum-weight matching ignores path
  degeneracy and, when X and Z components are decoded separately, ignores
  correlations such as a single Y fault producing both syndrome types.
  Thresholds cannot be quoted without the noise model, measurement model,
  circuit schedule, and decoder; the
  [threshold ledger](pedagogy/threshold-ledger.md) records those qualifiers.

- **Bias mismatch.** A square CSS patch gives equal X and Z distances even
  when the hardware does not. Rectangular patches or an XZZX basis align the
  protection with the channel.

- **No local non-Clifford gate.** Two-dimensional bounded-spread logical
  gates stop at the Clifford group. Universal computation therefore needs
  injection plus distillation, code switching, or another resource that
  leaves the theorem's assumptions.

- **Operations consume spacetime.** On a fixed planar patch architecture,
  lattice surgery is the usual two-qubit primitive because it preserves
  nearest-neighbor connectivity, but it is not the only one: defect braiding
  also works on fixed hardware, and stacked or movable layouts can expose
  transversal CNOT. “Every fixed-layout two-qubit gate is surgery” would be
  false.

## Operations story

**Transversal CNOT.** For two identical CSS blocks, pairwise physical CNOT
maps a control X-stabilizer to the product of corresponding control and target
X-stabilizers, and maps a target Z-stabilizer to the corresponding product in
the opposite direction. The same conjugation sends
`X_L⊗I → X_L⊗X_L` and `I⊗Z_L → Z_L⊗Z_L`. It is therefore a depth-one logical
CNOT when corresponding qubits can interact. Movable neutral-atom arrays
have demonstrated improvement of this two-qubit logical operation while
scaling surface-code distance from three to seven
([Bluvstein et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03982)); correlated errors still
require joint decoding. The transversal operation was the fault-tolerant
ingredient: preparation of the distance-five and distance-seven logical input
states was not itself fault-tolerant, so this result must not be read as an
end-to-end below-threshold memory demonstration.

**Lattice surgery.** Joining two smooth boundaries introduces local seam
checks whose product is `Z_L⊗Z_L`; the dual rough merge measures
`X_L⊗X_L`. A merge reduces `k` by one because the measured logical parity is
projected, and a split restores two output patches with a recorded Pauli
frame. Repeating the merged syndrome for `d` rounds supplies timelike
distance, but the fault-tolerant outcome comes from spacetime decoding, not
from a bare majority vote once data and circuit faults are allowed. The
[worked surgery page](pedagogy/lattice-surgery.md) derives the seam product,
checks the `L=3` rectangular merge as `n=28,k=1,d=3`, and separates the toy
measurement-only limit from the full decoder.

**Hadamard.** Applying H to every data qubit exchanges X and Z checks. For
this patch it maps the code to its dual, which is the same geometry rotated by
90 degrees. Transversal H followed by that relabeling is logical H. On fixed
hardware, restoring the original orientation is a distance-preserving code
deformation taking order `d` rounds
([Horsman et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.4022)).

**Folded Clifford gates.** If the surface code is maintained in a folded,
mirror-dual layout, paired qubits support a constant-depth logical S using
phase gates on the fold and CZ-type gates between mirror partners. The
logical gate is constant depth on an already folded layout; physically
folding or unfolding a planar patch is itself an order-`d` routing or
deformation operation. This distinction is explicit in
[Moussa's construction](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.02286).

**Braiding and twists.** Turning off checks creates holes. A loop around one
hole and a string between like holes form a logical pair; moving a primal
hole around a dual hole implements CNOT by code deformation. Boundary-type
changes create twists, whose braiding supplies single-qubit Clifford
operations. These are alternatives within the Clifford menu, not ways around
Bravyi–König.

**Universal completion.** Logical T is supplied by a non-stabilizer resource:
inject a noisy magic state, distill it using Clifford operations, and consume
it by gate teleportation. The operations listed in `card.yaml` distinguish
surgery, transversal, braiding, twist, and fold-transversal mechanisms so
that hardware geometry is never mistaken for an intrinsic property of the
code.

## Litmus questions

**Q1:** What single rank fact distinguishes this planar code from the toric
code? **A:** The open-chain repetition matrix is `(L−1)×L` with full row rank,
so its transpose code has dimension zero. Closing the chain creates one row
relation, making the transpose dimension one. In the HGP formula this changes
`1·1+0·0=1` into `1·1+1·1=2`.

**Q2:** Why is `d=L` a proof rather than a picture of one length-`L` string?
**A:** A length-`L` row and column prove only the upper bound. The lower bound
uses `L` disjoint representatives of each logical class: anything
anticommuting with the class must touch every representative, hence at least
`L` qubits. The representative equivalence and disjointness are checked in
[the distance transcript](pedagogy/distance-proof.md).

**Q3:** Why does XZZX reach 50% under pure dephasing while the CSS surface
code does not? **A:** Pure Z errors activate only one syndrome type in either
description. XZZX adds diagonal parity conservation, splitting that
two-dimensional problem into independent repetition codes. CSS lacks this
one-dimensional decomposition and retains its roughly 10.9% optimal
code-capacity threshold.

**Q4:** May one compare 10.9%, 2.9%, and 0.57% as three estimates of the same
threshold? **A:** No. They refer respectively to perfect-syndrome
code-capacity noise, repeated phenomenological data/measurement noise, and a
particular scheduled circuit-level model. Their elementary fault locations
and decoders differ. See the
[model-by-model ledger](pedagogy/threshold-ledger.md).

**Q5:** Why are `d` surgery rounds not simply “majority vote in time”?
**A:** If only independent seam-outcome flips occur, repeated parity samples
do reduce to a repetition code. Real syndrome circuits also contain data and
propagated faults, which create correlated spacetime detection events. The
logical parity is inferred jointly with those events by a spacetime decoder.

**Q6:** How many qubits does the unrotated patch consume when ancillas are
counted? **A:** It has `2d²−2d+1` data qubits and one fewer independent
checks, so one dedicated ancilla per check gives `4d²−4d+1` total. The
rotated totals are `d²` data plus `d²−1` ancillas, or `2d²−1`.

**Q7:** Is physical H on every qubit already a logical H? **A:** It exchanges
the code with its dual. The logical gate is transversal H plus the 90-degree
geometry relabeling; restoring a fixed planar footprint requires code
deformation. An S gate is constant depth only once the mirror-dual folded
layout is available.

**Q8:** What precisely forbids logical T? **A:** A bounded-depth,
bounded-range circuit on a growing-distance two-dimensional topological
Pauli stabilizer code induces a level-two Clifford-hierarchy operation.
`T` is level three. Injection and code switching work because they add a
resource or leave an assumption of that theorem.

**Physical route: gauge, close, then cut.**

1. The repetition/Ising code has a weight-one order parameter. Gauging its
   global `Z₂` symmetry gives edge qubits with star and plaquette constraints.
2. On an `L × L` torus there are `2L²` edge qubits. The `L²` stars have one
   product relation and so do the `L²` plaquettes, giving
   `k=2L²−(2L²−2)=2`. The logicals are the two homologically nontrivial loop
   classes and their duals.
3. A rough boundary condenses the electric endpoint of a Z string; a smooth
   boundary condenses the magnetic endpoint of an X string. A disk with only
   one boundary type has no protected string qubit. Alternating two rough and
   two smooth segments leaves a vertical Z class and a horizontal X class,
   which cross once and anticommute.
4. In the shipped geometry, top and bottom are rough and left and right are
   smooth. The [computed syndrome walk](pedagogy/syndrome-decoding.md) shows
   a bulk error producing two defects, a boundary absorbing one endpoint,
   and a completed crossing string producing no syndrome.

**Algebraic route: hypergraph product of two open chains.**

Let `H` be the `(L−1) × L` repetition parity matrix with adjacent `11`
rows. For two copies, the constructor forms

`H_X = [H ⊗ I_L | I_(L−1) ⊗ Hᵀ]`,

`H_Z = [I_L ⊗ H | Hᵀ ⊗ I_(L−1)]`.

The two qubit blocks contain `L²` bit×bit coordinates and `(L−1)²`
check×check coordinates. Commutation is designed in:

`H_X H_Zᵀ = H ⊗ Hᵀ + H ⊗ Hᵀ = 0` over `F₂`.

The open-chain matrix has rank `L−1`, hence classical dimensions
`k=1` and `kᵀ=0`. The HGP dimension formula
`k_Q=k₁k₂+k₁ᵀk₂ᵀ` therefore gives one logical qubit. Closing each chain
adds a dependent parity row: `kᵀ` becomes one and the same product gives the
toric code's two logical qubits. Thus “boundary versus handle” is the
corank of the classical factor matrix, not a metaphor.

The geometric checkerboard is exactly these Kronecker blocks laid out in the
plane. The [worked HGP page](pedagogy/hgp-construction.md) prints the matrices,
coordinate dictionary, locality checks, ranks, and commutation cancellation
from the shipped constructor.

## Multiple pictures

- **Homology.** `H_Zᵀ` and `H_X` are consecutive boundary maps. Z-logicals
  are relative cycles modulo face boundaries; X-logicals are the dual
  relative cycles. Multiplying by a stabilizer deforms a string within its
  relative homology class. Distance is the shortest nontrivial primal or dual
  relative cycle. See the
  [CSS chain-complex dictionary](../../foundations/css-chain-complexes/).

- **Anyons and decoding.** An error chain's syndrome is its boundary.
  Decoding chooses another chain with the same boundary; error plus
  correction is harmless exactly when the resulting cycle is homologically
  trivial. Maximum-likelihood decoding compares the total probability of
  homology classes, whereas minimum-weight matching keeps the lightest chain.
  The [syndrome page](pedagogy/syndrome-decoding.md) derives this statement,
  and the [threshold ledger](pedagogy/threshold-ledger.md) keeps the
  code-capacity, phenomenological, and circuit-level numbers separate.

- **Circuits and detectors.** A standard check measurement prepares one
  ancilla, entangles it with neighboring data qubits, and measures it. A
  detector is usually the parity of consecutive outcomes of the same check.
  Relevant single faults produce small detector patterns; some circuit faults
  are benign or observationally equivalent, so “every fault lights a
  detector” would be too strong. CNOT order matters because an ancilla fault
  can propagate to a two-data-qubit hook; the schedule must orient hooks away
  from the shortest logical direction.

- **Rotated cut.** The unrotated patch uses
  `2d²−2d+1` data qubits. Recutting the same bulk by 45 degrees puts the data
  on a `d × d` array while keeping both crossing lengths equal to `d`, giving
  `[[d²,1,d]]`. With one dedicated check ancilla per independent stabilizer,
  the totals are respectively `4d²−4d+1` and `2d²−1`. The saving is boundary
  geometry, not a new phase; the rotated construction is described explicitly
  in [Horsman et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.4022).

- **XZZX under biased noise.** A Hadamard on alternating data qubits maps the
  CSS presentation to XZZX checks. Under pure Z noise, XZZX defects obey
  separate parity constraints along diagonals, reducing decoding to
  independent repetition-code problems and giving a 50% code-capacity
  threshold. In the ordinary CSS presentation, pure Z errors trigger only
  X-checks—one syndrome graph—but that graph remains two-dimensional. The
  advantage is the XZZX diagonal conservation law, not a reduction from two
  CSS graphs to one. This mechanism and its finite-bias limits are derived in
  [Bonilla Ataides et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.07851).

- **Fermions and twists.** Star and plaquette defects are the `e` and `m`
  anyons. Moving one around the other produces a minus sign, so their
  composite has fermionic self-statistics. An `e↔m` duality wall can end at a
  twist defect; the patch corners are boundary-changing versions of the same
  object. This is why twist encodings inherit Majorana-like fusion
  bookkeeping without containing microscopic Majorana particles.

- **Laboratory memory.** Google's distance-five memory slightly outperformed
  distance three in the
  [2023 experiment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.06431). The later
  [distance-seven experiment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.13687) measured
  `0.143% ± 0.003%` logical error per cycle and an empirical suppression
  factor `Λ=2.14 ± 0.02` for a distance increase of two. `Λ` is a
  device-and-decoder fit, not a direct measurement of `p_th/p`.

## Why these parameters

**Length.** The HGP has one `L²` qubit block and one `(L−1)²` block, so
`n=2L²−2L+1`. The constructor and verifier recompute this for every shipped
instance.

**Dimension.** Each open repetition matrix has `k=1` and transpose dimension
zero. Künneth bookkeeping gives `1·1+0·0=1`. Direct rank computation agrees:
both quantum check matrices have rank `L(L−1)`, hence
`k=n−2L(L−1)=1`.

**Distance.** A row of the `L × L` block is an X-logical and a column is a
Z-logical, so `d≤L`. For the reverse inequality, the Z-logical class has `L`
pairwise-disjoint column representatives, all equivalent modulo
Z-stabilizers. Any logical anticommuting with that class must touch every one
of those disjoint supports and therefore has weight at least `L`; the same
argument with the X rows handles the conjugate class. Thus `d=L`. The
[distance page](pedagogy/distance-proof.md) proves the general statement and
then checks the representatives computationally.

**Verification status.** `L=3,4` use exhaustive CSS logical enumeration.
For `L=5`, the lower bound `d≥5` is carried by the family theorem and its
literature provenance, while the verifier reruns a seeded low-weight search
that finds a weight-five logical. The instance is therefore marked
`bounded`, not `verified`.

**Rate and locality.** `k/n→0` while `d=Θ(√n)`. This saturates the
two-dimensional `k d²=O(n)` tradeoff up to a constant. The complete argument,
including exactly where Euclidean bounded range enters, lives on the
[BPT derivation page](../../foundations/bounds/bravyi-poulin-terhal.md).
Likewise, the absence of a constant-depth local T gate follows from the
[full Bravyi–König derivation](../../foundations/bounds/bravyi-koenig.md),
not from a slogan about transversality.

## Failure modes

- **Area overhead.** For this unrotated family, one check ancilla per
  independent stabilizer gives `4d²−4d+1` physical qubits per logical
  memory. The rotated patch reduces this to `2d²−1`. These totals exclude
  routing lanes, spare qubits, and factory space, which must be stated
  separately rather than hidden in “physical qubits.”

- **No passive thermal memory.** A logical string can grow while paying only
  for its pointlike endpoints, so the commuting Hamiltonian has an
  order-one energy barrier. Two-dimensional local stabilizer Hamiltonians
  cannot be self-correcting
  ([Bravyi–Terhal](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.1983)); continuous active
  measurement is part of the memory, not an optional implementation detail.

- **Decoder/model dependence.** Minimum-weight matching ignores path
  degeneracy and, when X and Z components are decoded separately, ignores
  correlations such as a single Y fault producing both syndrome types.
  Thresholds cannot be quoted without the noise model, measurement model,
  circuit schedule, and decoder; the
  [threshold ledger](pedagogy/threshold-ledger.md) records those qualifiers.

- **Bias mismatch.** A square CSS patch gives equal X and Z distances even
  when the hardware does not. Rectangular patches or an XZZX basis align the
  protection with the channel.

- **No local non-Clifford gate.** Two-dimensional bounded-spread logical
  gates stop at the Clifford group. Universal computation therefore needs
  injection plus distillation, code switching, or another resource that
  leaves the theorem's assumptions.

- **Operations consume spacetime.** On a fixed planar patch architecture,
  lattice surgery is the usual two-qubit primitive because it preserves
  nearest-neighbor connectivity, but it is not the only one: defect braiding
  also works on fixed hardware, and stacked or movable layouts can expose
  transversal CNOT. “Every fixed-layout two-qubit gate is surgery” would be
  false.

## Operations story

**Transversal CNOT.** For two identical CSS blocks, pairwise physical CNOT
maps a control X-stabilizer to the product of corresponding control and target
X-stabilizers, and maps a target Z-stabilizer to the corresponding product in
the opposite direction. The same conjugation sends
`X_L⊗I → X_L⊗X_L` and `I⊗Z_L → Z_L⊗Z_L`. It is therefore a depth-one logical
CNOT when corresponding qubits can interact. Movable neutral-atom arrays
have demonstrated improvement of this two-qubit logical operation while
scaling surface-code distance from three to seven
([Bluvstein et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03982)); correlated errors still
require joint decoding. The transversal operation was the fault-tolerant
ingredient: preparation of the distance-five and distance-seven logical input
states was not itself fault-tolerant, so this result must not be read as an
end-to-end below-threshold memory demonstration.

**Lattice surgery.** Joining two smooth boundaries introduces local seam
checks whose product is `Z_L⊗Z_L`; the dual rough merge measures
`X_L⊗X_L`. A merge reduces `k` by one because the measured logical parity is
projected, and a split restores two output patches with a recorded Pauli
frame. Repeating the merged syndrome for `d` rounds supplies timelike
distance, but the fault-tolerant outcome comes from spacetime decoding, not
from a bare majority vote once data and circuit faults are allowed. The
[worked surgery page](pedagogy/lattice-surgery.md) derives the seam product,
checks the `L=3` rectangular merge as `n=28,k=1,d=3`, and separates the toy
measurement-only limit from the full decoder.

**Hadamard.** Applying H to every data qubit exchanges X and Z checks. For
this patch it maps the code to its dual, which is the same geometry rotated by
90 degrees. Transversal H followed by that relabeling is logical H. On fixed
hardware, restoring the original orientation is a distance-preserving code
deformation taking order `d` rounds
([Horsman et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.4022)).

**Folded Clifford gates.** If the surface code is maintained in a folded,
mirror-dual layout, paired qubits support a constant-depth logical S using
phase gates on the fold and CZ-type gates between mirror partners. The
logical gate is constant depth on an already folded layout; physically
folding or unfolding a planar patch is itself an order-`d` routing or
deformation operation. This distinction is explicit in
[Moussa's construction](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.02286).

**Braiding and twists.** Turning off checks creates holes. A loop around one
hole and a string between like holes form a logical pair; moving a primal
hole around a dual hole implements CNOT by code deformation. Boundary-type
changes create twists, whose braiding supplies single-qubit Clifford
operations. These are alternatives within the Clifford menu, not ways around
Bravyi–König.

**Universal completion.** Logical T is supplied by a non-stabilizer resource:
inject a noisy magic state, distill it using Clifford operations, and consume
it by gate teleportation. The operations listed in `card.yaml` distinguish
surgery, transversal, braiding, twist, and fold-transversal mechanisms so
that hardware geometry is never mistaken for an intrinsic property of the
code.

## Litmus questions

**Q1:** What single rank fact distinguishes this planar code from the toric
code? **A:** The open-chain repetition matrix is `(L−1)×L` with full row rank,
so its transpose code has dimension zero. Closing the chain creates one row
relation, making the transpose dimension one. In the HGP formula this changes
`1·1+0·0=1` into `1·1+1·1=2`.

**Q2:** Why is `d=L` a proof rather than a picture of one length-`L` string?
**A:** A length-`L` row and column prove only the upper bound. The lower bound
uses `L` disjoint representatives of each logical class: anything
anticommuting with the class must touch every representative, hence at least
`L` qubits. The representative equivalence and disjointness are checked in
[the distance transcript](pedagogy/distance-proof.md).

**Q3:** Why does XZZX reach 50% under pure dephasing while the CSS surface
code does not? **A:** Pure Z errors activate only one syndrome type in either
description. XZZX adds diagonal parity conservation, splitting that
two-dimensional problem into independent repetition codes. CSS lacks this
one-dimensional decomposition and retains its roughly 10.9% optimal
code-capacity threshold.

**Q4:** May one compare 10.9%, 2.9%, and 0.57% as three estimates of the same
threshold? **A:** No. They refer respectively to perfect-syndrome
code-capacity noise, repeated phenomenological data/measurement noise, and a
particular scheduled circuit-level model. Their elementary fault locations
and decoders differ. See the
[model-by-model ledger](pedagogy/threshold-ledger.md).

**Q5:** Why are `d` surgery rounds not simply “majority vote in time”?
**A:** If only independent seam-outcome flips occur, repeated parity samples
do reduce to a repetition code. Real syndrome circuits also contain data and
propagated faults, which create correlated spacetime detection events. The
logical parity is inferred jointly with those events by a spacetime decoder.

**Q6:** How many qubits does the unrotated patch consume when ancillas are
counted? **A:** It has `2d²−2d+1` data qubits and one fewer independent
checks, so one dedicated ancilla per check gives `4d²−4d+1` total. The
rotated totals are `d²` data plus `d²−1` ancillas, or `2d²−1`.

**Q7:** Is physical H on every qubit already a logical H? **A:** It exchanges
the code with its dual. The logical gate is transversal H plus the 90-degree
geometry relabeling; restoring a fixed planar footprint requires code
deformation. An S gate is constant depth only once the mirror-dual folded
layout is available.

**Q8:** What precisely forbids logical T? **A:** A bounded-depth,
bounded-range circuit on a growing-distance two-dimensional topological
Pauli stabilizer code induces a level-two Clifford-hierarchy operation.
`T` is level three. Injection and code switching work because they add a
resource or leave an assumption of that theorem.

documents.markdown:
# Surface code — Level-2 map

This is the index to the worked derivations, not a second intuition essay.
Each linked page answers one question completely and states which facts are
algebraic, recomputed, bounded, or literature-derived.

1. [Why HGP(rep_L, rep_L) is the unrotated planar patch](hgp-construction.md):
   the two qubit blocks, check matrices, CSS cancellation, geometry, locality,
   and `k=1`.
2. [Why the distance is exactly L](distance-proof.md): an upper-bound string,
   a disjoint-representative lower bound, exact enumeration at `L=3,4`, and the
   bounded `L=5` claim.
3. [Why syndrome is the boundary of an error chain](syndrome-decoding.md):
   bulk pairs, boundary condensation, the invisible completed string, detector
   histories, and what a decoder is deciding.
4. [Why a lattice-surgery seam measures logical parity](lattice-surgery.md):
   the telescoping seam product, merge dimension and distance, and why full
   fault tolerance uses spacetime decoding rather than bare majority vote.
5. [Which surface-code threshold a number refers to](threshold-ledger.md):
   a model-by-model provenance ledger that keeps code-capacity,
   phenomenological, circuit-level, and hardware numbers separate.

## Reproduction contract

Run from the repository root:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python atlas/surface/pedagogy/reproduce.py
make verify-entry E=atlas/surface
```

The same computation can be launched from a Python session:

```python
from runpy import run_path

run_path("atlas/surface/pedagogy/reproduce.py", run_name="__main__")
```

`reproduce.py` imports the shipped constructor and asserts every computed
statement used across these pages: check matrices, locality, ranks, logical
representatives, syndrome walk, exact distances, the seeded `L=5` upper
bound, resource counts, and the `L=3` rectangular surgery merge. It exits
nonzero on the first disagreement. The verifier independently reruns the
claims in `instances.yaml`.

The provenance split is deliberate:

- `n`, `k`, CSS structure, and the two small exact distances are
  machine-verified.
- The `L=5` lower bound is theorem/literature-backed; its upper bound is a
  seeded machine-rerunnable witness, so the instance is marked `bounded`.
- Thresholds and hardware results are not properties of a bare check matrix.
  They remain literature claims with the complete noise model and decoder
  written beside each number.

documents.title: The unrotated planar family has distance d=L
documents.markdown:
# The unrotated planar family has distance d=L

> **Theorem.** For the code `HGP(rep_L, rep_L)` with `L≥2`, every nontrivial
> logical Pauli has weight at least `L`, and weight-`L` X and Z logicals
> exist.

The proof does not infer distance from a drawing or from small-instance
enumeration.

## 1. Upper bound

Index the `L²` bit×bit block by `(a,b)`, `0≤a,b<L`.

- For fixed `a`, put X on all `(a,b)`. Each Z-check meets this row zero or two
  times, so the string commutes with every Z-check.
- For fixed `b`, put Z on all `(a,b)`. Each X-check likewise meets this column
  zero or two times.

A row and a column intersect once, so the two strings anticommute. Neither can
be a stabilizer. Both have weight `L`, proving `d≤L`.

## 2. Equivalent disjoint representatives

There are `L` row strings and `L` column strings. Adjacent X rows differ by
the product of the X-checks in the strip between them: interior qubits cancel
in pairs, leaving precisely the two boundary rows. Therefore all X rows
represent the same logical class. The same strip argument using Z-checks
makes all Z columns equivalent.

Within each family the supports are pairwise disjoint.

## 3. Lower bound

Because `k=1`, every nontrivial logical class is represented by
`X_L^a Z_L^b` with `(a,b)≠(0,0)`.

If a logical `P` anticommutes with the Z class, it anticommutes with every
equivalent Z-column representative: multiplying a representative by a
stabilizer cannot change its commutator with a logical. Anticommutation with a
pure-Z column requires `P` to have X or Y support somewhere on that column.
There are `L` disjoint columns, so `wt(P)≥L`.

If `P` instead anticommutes with the X class, the same argument uses the `L`
disjoint rows. Every nontrivial logical anticommutes with at least one of the
two conjugate classes, so every nontrivial logical has weight at least `L`.
Together with the upper bound, `d=L`.

This argument is the finite-patch version of a systolic proof: the disjoint
representatives form `L` independent cuts that every conjugate crossing must
meet.

## 4. Machine witnesses

At `L=3`, `reproduce.py` asserts the following facts:

```text
X rows logical/equivalent/disjoint: True
Z columns logical/equivalent/disjoint: True
logical X support: [0, 1, 2]
logical Z support: [0, 3, 6]
exact_distance(L=3): 3 (exact-css-enum)
```

At `L=4`, exhaustive CSS logical enumeration returns four. These are
`verified` claims in `instances.yaml`.

At `L=5`, exhaustive enumeration is not part of the verifier. The analytic
lower bound and
[Dennis–Kitaev–Landahl–Preskill](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0110143)
support `d≥5`; a deterministic low-weight search with
`method=rand-lowweight-v1`, `seed=0`, and `iters=2000` finds a weight-five
logical. The claim is therefore stored as

```yaml
property: d
lower: {value: 5}
upper: {value: 5, method: rand-lowweight-v1, seed: 0, iters: 2000}
origin: {kind: bounded, ref: dennis2002topological}
```

The word `bounded` is intentional: the theorem supplies the lower bound and
the verifier reruns the upper-bound witness, but the pipeline does not call
the result exhaustive.

documents.title: HGP(rep_L, rep_L) is the unrotated planar surface code
documents.markdown:
# HGP(rep_L, rep_L) is the unrotated planar surface code

> **Claim.** The shipped constructor produces local CSS checks on
> `n=L²+(L−1)²` qubits and encodes exactly one logical qubit.

Distance is intentionally deferred to
[its own proof](distance-proof.md). This page establishes the object and its
dimension.

## 1. The classical factor

Let `H=rep_parity(L)` be the `(L−1) × L` binary matrix

```text
1 1 0 0 ...
0 1 1 0 ...
      ...
... 0 1 1
```

Its rows are independent: beginning at the left edge, column zero occurs only
in row zero, so a zero linear combination forces the first coefficient to
vanish; repeating column by column forces every coefficient to vanish.
Therefore

`rank(H)=L−1`, `dim ker(H)=1`, and `dim ker(Hᵀ)=0`.

The one vector in `ker(H)` is the all-ones repetition word. The zero
transpose dimension is the algebraic signature of an open chain.

## 2. The quantum product

For two copies of `H`, the hypergraph product puts qubits in two blocks:

- bit×bit: `L²` qubits;
- check×check: `(L−1)²` qubits.

It defines

```text
H_X = [ H ⊗ I_L       | I_(L−1) ⊗ Hᵀ ]
H_Z = [ I_L ⊗ H       | Hᵀ ⊗ I_(L−1) ]
```

The CSS commutator has one contribution from each block:

```text
(H ⊗ I)(I ⊗ H)ᵀ       = H ⊗ Hᵀ
(I ⊗ Hᵀ)(Hᵀ ⊗ I)ᵀ     = H ⊗ Hᵀ
```

Their sum is zero over `F₂`. Block two is not decorative: it supplies the
second copy of the would-be commutation defect.

At `L=3`, the matrices asserted by the shipped computation are

```text
H_X =
100100000 | 1000
010010000 | 1100
001001000 | 0100
000100100 | 0010
000010010 | 0011
000001001 | 0001

H_Z =
110000000 | 1000
011000000 | 0100
000110000 | 1010
000011000 | 0101
000000110 | 0010
000000011 | 0001
```

Before reduction modulo two, every entry of `H_X H_Zᵀ` is either zero or two.
After reduction, all entries vanish.

## 3. Why the checks are geometrically local

Use the constructor's coordinates:

- bit×bit qubit `(a,b)` is at `(2b,2a)`;
- check×check qubit `(a,b)` is at `(2b+1,2a+1)`;
- X-check `(a,b)` is at `(2b,2a+1)`;
- Z-check `(a,b)` is at `(2b+1,2a)`.

Every `1` in a check row then joins sites at Manhattan distance exactly one.
Interior checks see four neighbors. At the left/right or top/bottom edge one
neighbor is absent, leaving weight three. `reproduce.py` checks this
adjacency for every shipped size, not only for the drawn `L=3` patch.

The `L=3` interleaved lattice is

```text
y=4  q6   Z4   q7   Z5   q8
y=3  X3   q11  X4   q12  X5
y=2  q3   Z2   q4   Z3   q5
y=1  X0   q9   X1   q10  X2
y=0  q0   Z0   q1   Z1   q2
```

Weight-three Z-checks lie on the top and bottom rough boundaries.
Weight-three X-checks lie on the left and right smooth boundaries.

## 4. Why `k=1`

There are `L(L−1)` rows in each quantum check matrix. The HGP rank identity
gives

```text
rank(H_X)
  = rank(H)L + (L−1)rank(H) − rank(H)²
  = L(L−1),
```

and the same for `H_Z`. Hence

```text
k = [L²+(L−1)²] − 2L(L−1) = 1.
```

Equivalently, the HGP dimension formula gives

```text
k_Q = k₁k₂ + k₁ᵀk₂ᵀ = 1·1 + 0·0 = 1.
```

If each open chain is closed into an `L`-edge cycle, the added parity row is
dependent. The ordinary kernel remains one-dimensional and the transpose
kernel becomes one-dimensional, giving `1·1+1·1=2`: the toric code.

## 5. Recompute it

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python atlas/surface/pedagogy/reproduce.py
```

The script asserts the matrix formulas, integer `{0,2}` cancellation,
nearest-neighbor geometry, and ranks for `L=3,4,5`.

documents.title: A seam of local checks measures logical parity
documents.markdown:
# A seam of local checks measures logical parity

> **Claim.** A smooth lattice-surgery merge measures `Z_L⊗Z_L` because the
> product of its new local Z-checks telescopes to that logical operator.

The dual rough merge measures `X_L⊗X_L`.

## 1. The `L=3` geometry

Place two unrotated distance-three patches side by side. Patch A occupies
`x=0,...,4`, patch B occupies `x=6,...,10`, and the missing seam is `x=5`.
Add the two horizontal seam data qubits at `(5,1)` and `(5,3)`, initialized
in `|+⟩`.

The old boundary X-stars extend across the seam. Their new X support has a
known `+1` contribution from the `|+⟩` seam qubits. Measure three new
Z-plaquettes centered at `(5,0)`, `(5,2)`, and `(5,4)`.

Multiplying those three outcomes cancels the two seam-qubit Z operators:
each appears in two neighboring plaquettes. What remains is

```text
Z(4,0) Z(4,2) Z(4,4) · Z(6,0) Z(6,2) Z(6,4),
```

the right-column representative of patch A's `Z_L` times the left-column
representative of patch B's `Z_L`. The product of local seam checks is
therefore the joint logical parity.

This is the content of lattice surgery: topology turns a nonlocal observable
into a product of simultaneously measured local checks
([Horsman et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.4022)).

## 2. Dimension and spacelike distance

Before the merge, the two patches have `26` data qubits and encode two
logical qubits. The two seam qubits give `n=28`. There are `27` independent
checks after the merge, so `k=1`: measuring one joint logical parity removes
one logical degree of freedom.

The merged patch is the rectangular product
`HGP(rep_3, rep_6)`. `reproduce.py` asks the engine for its exact parameters
and obtains

```text
n=28, k=1, independent checks=27, d=3
```

The long horizontal logical grows, while the short vertical logical remains
length three. Thus the merge preserves the original spacelike distance; it
does not magically turn the rectangle into distance six.

## 3. Why `d` rounds are needed

If the only possible fault were an independent flip of the inferred seam
parity in each round, repeating the parity and majority-voting would be a
one-dimensional repetition code in time.

That toy reduction is not the full fault-tolerance argument. Real extraction
circuits also contain data faults, ancilla propagation, and faults crossing
the start or end of the merge. They create correlated detection events in
space and time, and can change which representative of the joint logical
observable is being tracked. The merge syndrome must therefore be decoded as
one spacetime history. Running order `d` rounds supplies timelike distance;
the decoder, not a bare majority rule, combines seam and bulk detectors to
infer the logical parity.

## 4. Split and CNOT

To split, stop the seam checks and measure the seam data qubits in X. The
outcomes update the Pauli frame and restore two encoded patches.

A logical CNOT uses an ancilla patch prepared in `|+⟩`:

1. measure `Z_L^C Z_L^A`;
2. measure `X_L^A X_L^T`;
3. measure the ancilla logical Z;
4. classically track the outcome-dependent Pauli corrections.

Each joint measurement is the telescoping construction above, with X and Z
exchanged for the dual merge. The operation is Clifford and remains inside
the stabilizer formalism throughout.

documents.title: Syndrome is the boundary of an error chain
documents.markdown:
# Syndrome is the boundary of an error chain

> **Claim.** For a surface-code Pauli error chain `E`, the fired checks are
> exactly its boundary `∂E`. A correction succeeds precisely when error plus
> correction is a trivial relative cycle.

This single statement explains defect pairs, boundary nodes, matching, and
logical failure.

## 1. Algebra

Represent an X-error support by a binary vector `e_X`. The fired Z-checks are

`H_Z e_X`.

Each interior check sees the parity of incident error edges. Along a chain,
two incident segments cancel modulo two; only endpoints remain. The dual
statement sends a Z-error vector to `H_X e_Z`.

At a condensing boundary, a chain can end without a second physical check.
In a decoder graph this is represented by pairing the remaining defect to a
boundary node.

## 2. Computed `L=3` walk

The shipped constructor labels the central data qubit `q4` and a middle-row
crossing by `q3,q4,q5`. Direct matrix multiplication gives

```text
single X on q4          -> Z-checks {Z2, Z3}
single Z on q4          -> X-checks {X1, X4}
single X on left q3     -> Z-check  {Z2}
X on {q3,q4}            -> Z-check  {Z3}
X on {q3,q4,q5}         -> no fired checks
```

The last support is outside the X-stabilizer row space, so “no syndrome” means
a logical X, not a stabilizer. The sequence shows one defect entering at the
smooth boundary, walking across the patch, and disappearing at the opposite
smooth boundary.

## 3. What the decoder decides

Given a syndrome `s`, every candidate correction `C` satisfies
`∂C=s`. If the actual error is `E`, then

`∂(E+C)=s+s=0`.

Thus `E+C` is a cycle. Recovery succeeds if that cycle is a stabilizer
boundary and fails if it is a nontrivial relative homology class.

Minimum-weight matching chooses low-cost pairings of syndrome endpoints.
Maximum-likelihood decoding instead sums probabilities over all chains in
each logical class. That distinction is why path degeneracy can separate the
matching and optimal code-capacity thresholds; the exact model-dependent
numbers live in the [threshold ledger](threshold-ledger.md).

## 4. Repeated measurements

With noisy measurements, a detector compares the same check outcome in
successive rounds. Data faults create spacelike-separated detector events;
measurement faults create timelike-separated events; circuit propagation can
create correlated small patterns. Decoding therefore takes place in a
`2+1`-dimensional detector graph.

A relevant single fault has a bounded detector footprint, but not every
physical fault must light a detector: a late fault can be observationally
equivalent to a fault in the next round, a harmless Pauli can cancel, and
some faults affect only a tracked observable. The correct invariant is that
the detector error model lists the observable detector/logic signature of
each fault mechanism.

Ancilla faults deserve special attention. During a four-neighbor check
measurement, one ancilla Pauli can propagate through later CNOTs into a
two-data-qubit hook. A schedule that aligns those hooks with a shortest
logical direction can reduce circuit distance even though the static check
matrix still has distance `d`. Static-code distance and fault distance are
different claims and must be verified separately.

documents.title: Surface-code threshold ledger
documents.markdown:
# Surface-code threshold ledger

> **Rule.** A threshold number is meaningless without its elementary fault
> model, syndrome model, decoder, and normalization.

The regimes below are deliberately not merged into one “surface-code
threshold.”

### Code capacity, optimal

- **Model and decoder:** independent X or Z data errors, perfect syndrome,
  and class-probability/maximum-likelihood decoding.
- **Reported value:** about `10.9%`.
- **Provenance:** [Dennis–Kitaev–Landahl–Preskill](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0110143).

### Code capacity, minimum energy

- **Model and decoder:** the same perfect-syndrome setting, using the
  zero-temperature/minimum-chain approximation associated with matching.
- **Reported value:** `0.1031 ± 0.0001`.
- **Provenance:** [Wang–Harrington–Preskill](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0207088).

### Phenomenological spacetime

- **Model and decoder:** repeated data and syndrome errors in the
  random-plaquette gauge/matching model.
- **Reported value:** `0.0293 ± 0.0002` in the quoted symmetric convention.
- **Provenance:** [Wang–Harrington–Preskill](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0207088).

### Scheduled circuit

- **Model and decoder:** Fowler's specified eight-step syndrome circuit and
  per-step stochastic fault model.
- **Reported value:** `p_th=0.57%` per step, roughly `4%` per full eight-step
  cycle.
- **Provenance:** [Fowler–Mariantoni–Martinis–Cleland](https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.0928).

### Hardware fit

- **Model and decoder:** Google Willow rotated memories with the device's
  measured heterogeneous noise and real-time decoder.
- **Reported value:** `Λ=2.14 ± 0.02` per `d→d+2`; distance seven at
  `0.143% ± 0.003%` per cycle.
- **Provenance:** [Google Quantum AI, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.13687).

## 1. Why `10.9%` and `10.3%` differ

For a fixed syndrome, the probability of a logical class is a sum over all
error chains in that class. In the random-bond Ising mapping this is a
partition function. Optimal decoding compares free energies on the Nishimori
line. A minimum-chain decoder compares energies and discards most of the
entropy from nearly degenerate paths. The numerical gap is therefore a
decoder/statistical-mechanics distinction within one perfect-syndrome model,
not experimental uncertainty on one number.

## 2. Why `2.9%` is not a gate threshold

Adding noisy syndrome bits creates a time direction and a
three-dimensional matching/gauge problem. A phenomenological “data error per
round” and “measurement-bit flip per round” do not specify physical
preparation, CNOT, idle, leakage, reset, or readout locations. The resulting
threshold is valuable for decoder physics but cannot be compared directly
with a circuit-location threshold.

## 3. Why the `0.57%` conversion uses eight steps

The cited Fowler simulation defines `p` per step and explicitly uses eight
steps per cycle. Its quoted “roughly four percent per cycle” is the
conversion for that model. A different six-layer circuit may also be a valid
surface-code schedule, but one may not attach Fowler's eight-step conversion
to it without rebuilding the noise accounting.

## 4. Scaling below threshold

For simple independent models, the leading low-`p` logical failure mechanism
needs `⌈d/2⌉` faults, motivating an empirical form

`p_L ≈ A (p/p_th)^⌈d/2⌉`.

Increasing odd distance by two then contributes roughly one further factor
of `p/p_th`, before prefactors, degeneracy, correlations, and finite-size
effects. Hardware `Λ` is fitted from the complete device-and-decoder stack.
It should not be identified exactly with `p_th/p`.

## 5. Citation discipline

When a new threshold is added to the Atlas, record:

1. data-error channel;
2. whether syndrome is perfect, phenomenological, or circuit-derived;
3. complete circuit-location convention if applicable;
4. decoder and whether it uses correlations/degeneracy;
5. normalization: per location, step, round, cycle, or unit time.

Without those five fields, retain the number in the literature sweep rather
than promoting it into reader-facing content.
